result.summary: Completed 4,207,129 new physical training hands across four two-seed LR branches and 262,144 internal evaluation executions on 32,768 unique paired decks. Independent terminal review passed. Final half-minus-full was +8.6078 bb/100 in Seed1 and -10.9086 in Seed3, both nominal intervals crossing zero. Seed3 half-rate early improvement reversed: its parent-relative stage2-minus-stage1 change was -43.6969 [-67.0911,-20.3027]. No Slumbot or final-qualification hands were generated.
result.conclusion: Reducing the actual Adam LR halved mean PPO update KL and reduced early stops, but did not establish reproducible poker improvement or preservation. Original-rate endpoints were -2.3225 and -9.5087 bb/100 versus their fixed parents; half-rate endpoints were +6.2853 and -20.4172. The severe preregistered broad-collapse gate was false in both seeds, yet the curve does not support automatic larger allocation under the unchanged recipe. This is adverse/inconclusive internal scaling evidence, not proof that all full-representation learning fails at paper scale. Full-trainable scope still excludes direct preflop-actor and critic-v2 gradients to the shared representation. That contract observation is not a causal explanation of the losses.
result.decision: Do not select a learning-rate winner or automatically launch 4M/16M/paper-scale training. Retain both frozen final LR arms and both seeds. Before changing another training mechanism, calibrate these previously externally untested full-representation endpoints against Slumbot using a prospectively fixed 80k development allocation: all four policies receive 20k new hands each, regardless of interim scores. Existing internal/external ranking disagreement makes direct external calibration more decision-relevant than another proxy-only diagnostic or blindly extending this LR comparison.
result.next_step: Register and qualify a four-policy frozen external development calibration in a new experiment, reusing the established journaled CPU-greedy physical-v6/legacy-v4 bridge and audit/statistics machinery. Freeze all four current stage2 checkpoint hashes, runtime, distinct session IDs/policy seeds, balanced scheduling, 8x2500 hands per policy, no score-based stopping/extension/retry, raw/session uncertainty and multiplicity handling before any network request. Verify no live poker-owner overlap. After all 80k hands and evidence checks, assess external direction, severity and internal/external agreement before choosing further scale or a single-change general training control. A preflop actor-to-representation gradient-route control remains a hypothesis, not an adopted fix. No Slumbot labels/action rules, no final qualification credit, and no new training in that calibration.

experiments.title: Static-current-KL 262k-to-1M high-pot critic calibration
experiments.benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
experiments.hypothesis: Across fresh internal common-deck play against four general anchors and both seats, the 1M endpoints have a replicated high-pot-specific critic calibration degradation relative to their seed-matched 262k parents.
experiments.material_change: Zero-Slumbot read-only on-policy critic calibration audit using first decision per pot bucket, matched common-reach hand identities, and a preregistered high-minus-low difference-in-differences gate; no weights or action rules change.
experiments.baseline: The 1M scale evaluation had a noisy positive pooled internal slope (+0.4358 bb/100, raw pair CI [-3.0908,3.9625]) but only one of three seeds met breadth. Existing Slumbot attribution localized replicated losses to final pots >=30bb without causal action support.
experiments.source: Seed-matched v6-static-current-kl 262k and 1M frozen endpoints, plus Standard10, CFR4, legacy iter16, and legacy mixed65k anchors.
notes: Preflight before record start: py_compile PASS; 3 unit tests PASS; separate 96-hand CPU smoke PASS. Smoke outputs are outside the experiment directory and are not scientific evidence.
All 6,144 generated decks were unique and disjoint from 98,304 prior raw static-current-KL lineage deck digests. Checkpoint SHA256 values were unchanged after evaluation.

The three treatment high-pot residual biases were all optimistic in sign (-9.05,-7.80,-6.02 bb for target minus prediction), but every per-seed 95% CI included zero. This descriptive pooled tendency does not satisfy the preregistered multi-seed significance gate.

result.summary: The fresh 24,576-hand internal calibration audit completed with 590 common-reach high-pot identities. The 1M endpoints did not have higher high-pot error than their 262k parents: pooled squared-error delta was -223.94 bb^2 with CI95 [-531.66,83.78], and high-minus-low difference-in-differences was -103.50 with CI95 [-252.44,45.44].
result.conclusion: The externally localized >=30bb loss class does not close a causal loop through worsening internal critic calibration. Error worsening appeared in only one seed, high-pot specificity pointed negative, and no treatment seed had a significant residual bias. Do not oversample high-pot states, reset the critic, reverse actions, or imitate solver/Slumbot labels from this evidence.
result.next_step: Return to geometric scale evidence for the preserved static-current-KL method. Its 262k-to-1M internal slope was positive in two of three seeds with low drift and no replicated mechanism failure; preregister a multi-seed 1M-to-4M continuation with intermediate 2M checkpoints and untouched broad internal evaluation, rather than opening a benchmark-specific patch.

experiments.title: Integrated 1M/2M Slumbot loss attribution with held-out solver proxy
experiments.benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
experiments.hypothesis: A small set of general hand/state classes explains a replicated share of the 1M and 2M external losses across independent sessions, and at least one such class also has elevated disagreement from high-confidence Standard10+CFR4 consensus on held-out matched final states.
experiments.material_change: Zero-new-Slumbot hand-level discovery/confirmation attribution over the two audited 20k cohorts, followed by a label-free Standard10+CFR4 matched-state proxy gate; no learned weights or benchmark-specific rules are changed.
experiments.baseline: Seed1 1M scored -21.7592 bb/100 CI95 [-44.2479,0.7295]; Seed1 2M scored -38.02 CI95 [-59.4244,-16.6156]. Prior outcome-blind replay rejected simple Standard10-distance attribution, and bounded public-objective MGDA failed untouched breadth translation.
experiments.source: Audited raw hands from v6-integrated-seed1-1m-greedy-fresh20k-slumbot-20260903 and v6-integrated-seed1-2m-greedy-fresh20k-slumbot-20260903 plus CPU-exact state replay from v6-integrated-1m-2m-slumbot-state-drift-20260903.
notes: Sessions1-4 are discovery and sessions5-8 untouched confirmation in each corpus. Candidate classes are fixed in preregistration. Outcome tails are descriptive only; no Slumbot action or reward becomes a training target. Proxy support additionally requires elevated disagreement from high-confidence Standard10+CFR4 consensus in both confirmation corpora.

Post-hoc robustness, not used to change the preregistered decision: every leave-one-confirmation-session-out high-pot effect remained negative in both corpora. Approximate independent-binomial disagreement-uplift CIs were [+0.0267,+0.0624] at 1M and [+0.0151,+0.0475] at 2M.

The 39 high-confidence teacher-consensus disagreements in confirmed high-pot states were almost entirely on-policy all-in versus teacher check/call. Their observed outcome direction did not replicate: 1M had 24 hands net -70 bb, while 2M had 15 hands net +570 bb. This forbids interpreting the teacher action as a causal correction or using it as an action label.

result.summary: Across two independent 20k external cohorts, final-decision pots at least 30bb concentrated replicated losses and elevated high-confidence Standard10+CFR4 consensus disagreement. The preregistered class gate passed for this one class; all fold-related correlations failed the solver proxy.
result.conclusion: Large-pot states are a credible general coverage/value-calibration risk class: their negative excess survives every leave-one-session-out check and the policy differs from two general teachers more often there. However the specific all-in-versus-check/call discrepancy has opposite observed outcomes across 1M and 2M, so no action reversal, Slumbot label imitation, or direct solver-teacher patch is justified. The result localizes where to test internal critic calibration, not what action to take.
result.next_step: On fresh internal matched deals across multiple general opponents and both seats, measure terminal-return critic calibration and policy regret proxies stratified by pot/exposure, with special emphasis on final pots at least30bb. Compare the retained static-current-KL 1M endpoints with their parents and Standard10; only train a general high-pot resampling or value-calibration intervention if the internal defect replicates independently of Slumbot outcomes.

result.next_step: Do not revive entropy sharpening, greedy-margin, direct-greedy ES, or 25%-public-opponent training, which have explicit negative evidence. result.summary: Nine frozen archive evaluations completed over 73,728 hands. All 18,432 raw pair rows passed SHA, count, uniqueness, common-deck, and identical-control gates. The paired 149k-to-262k pooled change averaged -1.947 bb/100 across seeds with t95 CI [-17.051, 13.157]; Standard10 and CFR4 contrasts were also inconclusive.
result.conclusion: The preregistered selective Standard10 tradeoff hypothesis is rejected: neither key anchor has a coherent monotone curve, there is no statistically coherent broad decline or positive curve, and two of three lineages flip final common-anchor sign across independent fresh panels. Current approximately1k-pair-per-anchor frozen panels expose high between-deal and between-seed variance, not a mechanism-level reason to terminate a potentially long-horizon recipe.
result.next_step: Continue only Seed1, the sole lineage that passed the original 262k breadth and both-seat gate, from its exact 263,423-hand state to 1,048,576 actual hands. Preserve optimizer/replay/league/assignment state and use a nonoverlapping deal window; then require a larger frozen four-anchor both-seat panel before any replication or Slumbot spend.

All three pooled slopes were positive and final holdout/seat medians were positive, but seed1 final holdout (-29.232) and correct-vs-wrong context value (-10.16) were negative. Admission is therefore to one monitored geometric continuation, not evidence of uniform OOD improvement.

result.summary: Three continuous posterior-context seeds completed 20,736 training and 27,648 evaluation hands. From 128 to 512 learning hands/group, pooled slopes were +11.874, +19.192, and +10.855 bb/100; final deltas were +3.902, +16.414, +10.247. Final holdout median was +11.263 and seat median +9.683. Exact replay verified all six trajectories, schedules, checkpoints, optimizer states, and 384/384 positive-geometry updates.
result.conclusion: The reliability-shrunk posterior-context method now has a reproducible positive geometric learning slope, multi-seed breadth medians, strong Standard10 preservation, and exact training provenance. One seed exhibits severe holdout tradeoff, so the next 4x continuation must keep per-seed holdout and context-value gates rather than relying only on pooled performance.
result.next_step: Resume the three exact endpoint512 checkpoints, optimizers, and group counts to 2,048 learning hands/group without replaying prior hands. Save geometry in each new checkpoint, evaluate on larger fresh broad common-deck cohorts, and require at least two positive slopes plus at least two nonnegative final holdout seeds before any further scale or Slumbot gate.

experiments.title: Frozen entropy-reliability contextual shrinkage fresh control
experiments.benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
experiments.hypothesis: The fixed outcome-blind multiplier 1 - posterior_entropy/log(6) will preserve nonnegative training-domain and both-seat performance while repairing unseen breadth: both frozen seeds and both seats remain nonnegative versus Standard10, holdout shrunk-minus-base is nonnegative, and shrinkage improves holdout reward versus the unshrunk checkpoint on fresh common decks.
experiments.material_change: Add inference-only posterior reliability power=1 without changing learned tensors. Hash-load both frozen recovery checkpoints and the classifier, generate wholly fresh 64-hand contexts and 128 common-deck pairs for every nine-policy/two-seat cell, and compare Standard10, unshrunk, and reliability-shrunk arms. No reward-based multiplier search and no training updates.
experiments.baseline: Unshrunk checkpoints were positive across seeds/seats but pooled holdout delta was -1.302 ±7.491 bb/100. Independent sealed features showed reliability mean 0.583 seen versus 0.349 unseen with AUC 0.799.
notes: Power=1 is fixed from the outcome-blind feasibility result. The control will not scan powers or select checkpoints from these rewards. Paired-deck units average seats before primary CIs.

Both 8,064-hand seed evidence files completed before a postprocessing-only failure. The original aggregation omitted seed_index from its pair key; recovery added seed_index and recomputed all metrics from unchanged SHA-frozen JSONL with zero regenerated hands.

All preregistered pooled gates passed, but seed1 holdout was unchanged by shrinkage and remained -0.456 bb/100. Therefore the multiplier is admitted as a conservative OOD control, not as replicated holdout improvement.

result.summary: Across 16,128 fresh evaluation hands, fixed entropy reliability changed the two frozen policies from pooled -3.792 bb/100 unshrunk to +3.472 ±4.920 shrunk. Holdouts improved from -13.125 to +0.879 ±5.226 and training domains remained +4.769; both seeds and seats had nonnegative shrunk pooled point estimates.
result.conclusion: Outcome-blind entropy shrinkage materially reduces OOD downside while preserving the learned contextual signal. Its effect is seed-heterogeneous, so it supports a conservative geometric learning-curve expansion with multiple seeds and frozen checkpoints, not a strength claim or Slumbot gate.
result.next_step: Train three new posterior-centered seeds on a preregistered 4x geometric curve with frozen checkpoints at the current 128 and 512 learning-hands-per-group doses; evaluate every endpoint with reliability power=1 on new broad common decks, tracking seed slopes, holdout breadth, both seats, and Standard10 preservation.

experiments.title: Outcome-blind context entropy reliability feasibility
experiments.benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
experiments.hypothesis: The calibrated classifier's normalized posterior reliability (1 - entropy/log6) separates untouched seen-policy sessions from SHA-disjoint unseen-policy sessions strongly enough to gate residual magnitude without reward tuning: seen median at least 0.40, holdout median at most 0.40, mean gap at least 0.15, and discrimination AUC at least 0.75.
experiments.material_change: Hash-freeze the 84 session-feature rows and admitted regularized 64-hand classifier. Compute entropy reliability on the original 48 selection, 24 untouched seen-test, and 12 unseen holdout sessions; use no rewards, policy checkpoints, or environment simulation.
experiments.baseline: Posterior-centered learned heads improved seen policies but were -1.302 ±7.491 bb/100 versus Standard10 on unseen holdouts. An entropy multiplier is only justified if classifier uncertainty independently distinguishes those domains.
notes: Thresholds are preregistered before reading the sealed reliability outputs. Passing admits only a fresh shrinkage control, not strength.
Reliability thresholds were fixed before querying the sealed 24 seen-test and 12 SHA-disjoint holdout sessions. No reward, policy checkpoint, or environment hand was read or generated.

result.summary: Normalized posterior reliability separated seen and unseen 64-hand contexts: seen mean/median 0.583/0.584 versus unseen 0.349/0.296, a mean gap of 0.234 and AUC 0.799. All preregistered feasibility gates passed.
result.conclusion: Classifier entropy contains independently validated OOD information and supports a deterministic learned-policy uncertainty multiplier. This admits exactly one fresh matched shrinkage control; it does not establish poker strength or justify selecting a multiplier from reward outcomes.
result.next_step: Implement the fixed multiplier 1 - posterior_entropy/log(6), verify zero-context/uniform-posterior identity, then evaluate both frozen recovery checkpoints on fresh common decks against base and the unshrunk policy across training and holdout opponents.

experiments.title: Posterior-context raw paired-deck breadth audit
experiments.benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
experiments.hypothesis: The two positive pooled seeds should remain directionally consistent after independent paired-deck reconstruction across seats and should not be concentrated in seen domains: both seats, the holdout split, at least two of three holdout opponents, and correct-versus-wrong deltas in both splits should be nonnegative before geometric training expansion.
experiments.material_change: Hash-verify both raw evaluation JSONL artifacts, discard warmup rows, reconstruct 1,152 independent common-deck units by averaging the two hero seats, and recompute CIs by seed, training/holdout split, opponent, and seat for correct-minus-base and correct-minus-wrong. Generate no hands and update no weights.
experiments.baseline: Both recovery seeds passed pooled gates (+6.574/+2.235 versus base), but their separate holdout deltas were -0.651/-1.953 bb/100 and therefore require breadth analysis before scaling.
notes: Paired-deck units, not individual seat rows, are the primary CI unit. The audit is frozen and cannot select or modify checkpoints.
Primary inference used 1,152 common-deck units formed by averaging both hero seats before computing confidence intervals. All source JSONL hashes matched and warmup rows were excluded.

result.summary: Independent raw reconstruction found pooled correct-context improvement +4.405 bb/100 (95% CI -1.935 to +10.744) and correct-versus-wrong +8.129 (CI -0.949 to +17.207). Both seeds and seats were positive. Training domains were +7.258, while SHA-disjoint holdouts were -1.302 ±7.491; two of three holdout opponents were nonnegative.
result.conclusion: Posterior-centered conditioning is reproducibly active and not seat-concentrated, but its small apparent gain is concentrated in seen styles. Holdout evidence is uncertain rather than catastrophic, yet it fails the preregistered breadth condition, so geometric training expansion is premature. An outcome-blind uncertainty-shrinkage feasibility check is warranted before new evaluation hands.
result.next_step: Using the frozen calibrated classifier and sealed session features only, compare posterior reliability distributions for seen versus SHA-disjoint contexts and quantify whether entropy-based shrinkage preserves seen conditioning while materially reducing unseen residual magnitude; generate no hands.

experiments.title: Posterior-centered contextual MGDA group-support recovery
experiments.benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
experiments.hypothesis: With the brittle group batch reduced a priori from 64 to 32, the posterior-centered architecture will complete two new independent seeds while reproducing the first attempt's mechanism: preserved Standard10, positive MGDA geometry, nonnegative median correct-context delta, and positive median correct-versus-mismatched-context delta.
experiments.material_change: Repeat the failed attempt on two wholly new seeds with the sole learning-config correction group_batch_size=32. Persist each seed's 2,304 raw training hands before support validation or optimization and report all twelve decision supports; retain the exact classifier, architecture, warmup, learning-hand, step, and evaluation budgets.
experiments.baseline: The failed attempt's only completed seed preserved 99.66% of active-context Standard10 actions and scored +3.115 bb/100 versus base and +19.568 bb/100 versus wrong context, but seed1 lacked 64 decision rows in one group and could not test replication.
notes: The failed attempt remains immutable and is not counted as a completed replication. This recovery uses new seeds and a fixed lower support threshold, not adaptive post hoc batch sizing.
All twelve group decision supports were persisted; the minimum was 68, safely above the fixed batch size 32. Both independent optimizer states and all raw hand/schedule artifacts are hash recorded.

The preregistered pooled mechanism gates passed, but both seeds were negative versus Standard10 on SHA-disjoint holdout opponents. This admits context-dependent learning, not broad generalization or a scale promotion without a pooled breadth audit.

result.summary: The corrected two-seed posterior-centered smoke completed 4,608 training and 9,216 evaluation hands. Both seeds were positive overall versus base (+6.574, +2.235 bb/100) and versus mismatched context (+15.673, +0.586), with 99.61-99.90% Standard10 agreement and 100% positive MGDA geometry.
result.conclusion: Zero-mean posterior heads reproducibly repair the raw architecture's inactive-conditioning failure while strongly preserving Standard10. However, improvement is concentrated in seen training domains: both independent holdout deltas are slightly negative and uncertain. The mechanism is admitted, but evidence is not yet broad enough for geometric training expansion.
result.next_step: Pool and independently recompute both seeds' raw evaluation rows by opponent, split, and seat; audit correct-vs-base and correct-vs-wrong CIs and concentration. Scale only if breadth is not contradicted; otherwise revise the OOD posterior shrinkage before more training.

experiments.title: Posterior-centered contextual residual MGDA smoke
experiments.benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
experiments.hypothesis: Replacing the generic-dominated raw interaction with a frozen calibrated six-style posterior and zero-mean learned head mixture will produce reproducible context-dependent policy behavior: both seeds retain the preservation/geometry contracts, conditioning heads update, and the median correct-context policy both remains nonnegative versus Standard10 and beats cyclically mismatched context.
experiments.material_change: Use the exact hash-frozen admitted 64-hand L2=1/temperature=1.1892 classifier. The trainable residual is a posterior-weighted mixture of six state-conditioned policy heads after subtracting the uniform posterior, structurally forbidding a shared generic delta; zero context and uniform posterior remain exact Standard10. Repeat the parent's two-seed 4,608 training-hand and 9,216 three-arm evaluation budget on new seeds.
experiments.baseline: The raw-interaction parent had contextual/generic logit ratios 16.0% and 8.25%, under 0.1% context action disagreement, and exactly zero correct-vs-wrong reward difference despite stable MGDA updates.
notes: This is an architecture-mechanism control at small scale. A clear failure to produce context-dependent actions rejects this formulation; noisy absolute reward alone will not be treated as asymptotic evidence.

Seed0 completed and its checkpoint plus raw training/evaluation/schedule evidence are preserved. Seed1 generated 2,304 environment training hands but failed before update because at least one opponent-seat group had fewer than 64 hero-decision rows; its in-memory rows were not persisted by the pre-recovery trainer. No artifact was overwritten.

Seed0's +3.115 bb/100 versus base and +19.568 bb/100 correct-versus-wrong are promising mechanism evidence only. They are not accepted as a two-seed result and will not be used for strength promotion.

result.summary: The posterior-centered architecture completed seed0 with genuine context dependence and 99.66% Standard10 agreement, then the run stopped safely at seed1's pre-update support gate. Only one of two seeds is complete, so the experiment is failed for infrastructure rather than scientific rejection.
result.conclusion: The zero-mean posterior head design repaired the parent's inactive-context symptom in seed0, but the planned two-seed test is incomplete. A brittle without-replacement group batch of 64 exceeded one seed's collected hero-decision support; the correct response is a fresh matched recovery with a lower fixed batch and earlier evidence persistence.
result.next_step: Persist each seed's raw training evidence before optimization, report exact per-group supports, and rerun two wholly new seeds with fixed group_batch_size=32 while preserving all other budgets and gates.

experiments.title: Frozen contextual residual logit-sensitivity audit
experiments.benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
experiments.hypothesis: The two stable but greedy-inactive contextual checkpoints may contain opponent-conditioned sub-argmax logit signal. Across 2,048 balanced states and twelve distinct saved 64-hand contexts per seed, mean contextual logit RMS should exceed 1e-4 and at least 10% of generic residual RMS; if so, a controlled dose increase is informative even if current greedy actions are invariant.
experiments.material_change: Without generating hands or updating weights, hash-verify both frozen checkpoints and raw training evidence, recover each group's final saved context, and query every state under all twelve contexts. Decompose generic versus contextual residual RMS, action disagreement, base-margin crossing slack, and street-seat partitions.
experiments.baseline: The parent smoke updated both context encoders and changed 0.195% of active-context Standard10 actions, but correct versus cyclically mismatched context produced exactly identical greedy rewards in both seeds.
notes: This audit selects no checkpoint and touches no policy weights. Its purpose is to distinguish a clear inactive-conditioning mechanism from a sub-argmax signal that may rationally merit geometric dose scaling.
All 49,152 state-context queries were frozen and outcome-blind. The twelve final group contexts per seed were recovered from hash-verified raw learning-hand evidence and were mutually distinct.

result.summary: Across 2,048 balanced states and twelve saved contexts per checkpoint, contextual logit RMS was nonzero but small: 0.000984/0.000605 versus generic RMS 0.00615/0.00733. Context-to-generic ratios were 16.0% and 8.25%, greedy context disagreement only 0.049% and 0.098%, and margin crossing below 0.2%.
result.conclusion: The raw multiplicative architecture learns mostly a generic residual and only weak, non-replicated conditional variation. Blindly scaling its current recipe is not supported. This is a mechanism-level architecture/objective diagnosis, independent of the small run's absolute reward.
result.next_step: Use the admitted calibrated 64-hand classifier as a frozen six-style posterior and train a zero-mean posterior-centered bank of learned policy heads, which structurally forbids a generic residual while retaining exact Standard10 at zero context; rerun a matched two-seed mechanism smoke.

experiments.title: Standard10-preserving 64-hand contextual residual MGDA smoke
experiments.benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
experiments.hypothesis: A learned state-by-public-context residual can exploit the admitted 64-hand opponent signal while preserving Standard10: across two seeds, MGDA retains positive worst-group geometry on at least 75% of updates, active-context source agreement remains at least 95% overall/90% every street-seat partition, zero context is exactly base, and the median correct-context policy delta is nonnegative and exceeds the same learned policy under mismatched context.
experiments.material_change: Add a 20-feature cross-hand context encoder interacting multiplicatively with native-v6 state features and a hard architectural zero-context identity gate. For each of twelve training opponent-seat groups and two seeds, collect 64 Standard10 warmup hands plus 128 contextual learning hands, train 32 broad MGDA steps, then compare frozen base/correct-context/mismatched-context arms on common decks across all six training and three SHA-disjoint holdout policies.
experiments.baseline: Regularized context classification passed at 64 hands (91.67% untouched accuracy, 75% minimum-class, 65.11% normalized unseen-policy entropy), but no learned poker policy has yet consumed that context. Prior context-free broad MGDA preserved Standard10 but had weak/noisy holdout improvement.
notes: This is a small mechanism smoke, not a verdict on asymptotic learning. Failure of implementation/preservation/context-use gates rejects the mechanism; noisy early reward without a mechanistic failure is undertraining evidence and will be judged using cross-seed and correct-vs-mismatched alignment.
Both seeds completed exact independent hand streams and nonempty optimizer states. All MGDA worst-group alignments were positive and zero-context remained exactly Standard10.

Correct-context and cyclically mismatched-context greedy rewards were exactly identical in every evaluated hand for both seeds. This is a concrete inactive-conditioning mechanism result at the current 32-step/128-learning-hands-per-group dose, not an asymptotic rejection based on the negative absolute reward of a small run.

result.summary: Two contextual residual seeds completed 4,608 environment training hands and 9,216 three-arm evaluation hands. Geometry and preservation were sound (99.80% active-context Standard10 agreement), but correct versus mismatched context produced exactly 0 bb/100 in both seeds; base deltas were +0.217 and -2.648 bb/100.
result.conclusion: The architecture trains stably and preserves the external Standard10 prior, yet the current dose does not produce context-dependent greedy behavior. The reward evidence therefore does not justify geometric scaling until a frozen logit-level audit determines whether context signal exists below the argmax boundary or is being ignored by learned weights.
result.next_step: Run a zero-new-hand frozen sensitivity audit over balanced states and all saved 64-hand contexts, measuring logit variance, pairwise context action disagreement, margin crossing distance, and seed consistency before choosing dose or architecture changes.

experiments.title: Nested-CV opponent-context regularization control
experiments.benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
experiments.hypothesis: The failed minimum-class and OOD-calibration gates arise mainly from the unregularized readout rather than insufficient public session features; session-index-disjoint cross-validation can select L2 and temperature without touching the final test, yielding at 64 hands at least 75% overall accuracy, 50% every-class accuracy, and 25% normalized entropy on SHA-disjoint unseen policies.
experiments.material_change: Reuse the exact hash-frozen 84 session-feature rows with zero new environment hands. Select L2 by eight-fold session-index OOF minimum-class accuracy then overall accuracy and NLL; select temperature only by OOF NLL; fit on all 48 selection rows and open the 24 untouched test plus 12 unseen holdout rows exactly once.
experiments.baseline: The unregularized readout reached 79.17% aggregate 64-hand accuracy but only 25% minimum-class accuracy and 0.00368 nats holdout entropy with 100% training accuracy.
notes: The 24 final test rows and 12 unseen-policy rows are sealed from hyperparameter and temperature selection. Passing this readout gate would admit a context representation mechanism only, not policy strength.

No new poker hands were generated. Model and temperature selection used only 48 selection sessions; 24 test sessions and 12 SHA-disjoint holdout sessions remained untouched until the final evaluation.

At 32 hands, overall accuracy passed but minimum-class accuracy remained 25%; any downstream policy prototype must treat the first 32 hands as insufficient context and preserve the base policy under uncertainty.

result.summary: Nested session-index CV selected L2=1 and temperature=1.1892 at 64 hands. The single untouched test reached 91.67% overall accuracy and 75% minimum-class accuracy, while SHA-disjoint holdout normalized entropy rose to 65.11%; all preregistered gates passed with zero new environment hands.
result.conclusion: Strong regularization and OOF-only calibration resolve the prior readout's breadth failure at 64 hands, so public cross-hand context is admitted as a feasible representation mechanism. The 32-hand minimum-class failure bounds the useful horizon, and no poker-policy strength claim follows from classifier accuracy alone.
result.next_step: Build a minimal Standard10-preserving context-conditioned learned residual pilot across multiple seeds and both seats, with a strict zero-context equivalence gate and untouched broad-league evaluation before any Slumbot use or geometric scaling.

experiments.title: Public cross-hand opponent-context feasibility
experiments.benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
experiments.hypothesis: A compact outcome-independent public action context accumulated across hands can identify the six heterogeneous broad-league opponent styles on fresh sessions (at least 50% accuracy by 32 hands and 75% by 64, with every class at least 50%), supporting a context-conditioned learned policy that can specialize without benchmark-specific rules.
experiments.material_change: Generate deterministic 64-hand sessions with frozen Standard10 hero against six training and three SHA-disjoint holdout policies. Build only public street-by-action rates and activity counts, fit horizon-specific linear classifiers on eight sessions per training policy, evaluate on four untouched sessions per policy and unseen holdout sessions, and save raw decks/actions. No Slumbot and no policy-strength claim.
experiments.baseline: Existing shared residual gradients conflict across opponent-seat groups, while MGDA/CAGrad and direct-greedy ES did not yield scalable directions. Current policies observe only within-hand history and cannot carry opponent evidence across hands.
notes: The 3,072 training hands are environment hands used only to form session-level representation examples; no policy weights were trained and no Slumbot hands were used.

The aggregate 64-hand accuracy gate passed, but the preregistered minimum-class breadth gate failed (25% versus 50%). Unseen-policy entropy near zero reveals severe OOD overconfidence. This rejects only the raw unregularized classifier, not cross-hand context universally.

result.summary: Frozen Standard10 generated 84 deterministic 64-hand public-only sessions across six training and three SHA-disjoint holdout policies. The linear classifier reached 62.5% at 32 hands and 79.17% at 64 hands on untouched training-policy sessions, but minimum per-class accuracy was only 25% and unseen holdout predictions were pathologically overconfident.
result.conclusion: Public cross-hand action counts contain aggregate opponent-style signal, but the current unregularized linear readout fails breadth and OOD calibration. It is unsafe to condition a learned poker policy on this representation as implemented. The result is a mechanism-level rejection of the raw readout, not evidence that cross-hand adaptation is intrinsically unlearnable or undertraining evidence about a policy.
result.next_step: Reuse the frozen session-feature evidence in a zero-new-hand nested-CV L2 and temperature-calibration control; keep the existing untouched test sessions sealed until model selection is complete.

experiments.title: Greedy ES direction SNR 32-to-128-pair scale control
experiments.benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
experiments.hypothesis: The negative split-half direction correlation at 32 pairs per opponent is estimator under-sampling rather than intrinsically unlearnable signal; extending the exact same zero-center, sigma0.8 directions and deck prefixes to 128 pairs per opponent will make half and mean quarter rank correlations positive and stabilize at least four of eight direction signs.
experiments.material_change: Freeze the exact prior center, random-feature model seed, eight normalized directions, sigma, six training opponents, seats, and pair0-31 evidence. Generate only pair32-127 supplements, then recompute direction fitness on four disjoint 32-pair quarters, two 64-pair halves, and the full 128-pair cohort. Do not update weights or run validation/Slumbot.
experiments.baseline: At 32 pairs per opponent, all eight directions activated but independent 16-pair halves had Pearson correlation -0.6313 and the resulting center validation slope was -21.35 +/-41.85 bb/100. This control tests sample efficiency, not strength.

result.summary: The fixed-center sigma0.8 ES direction cohort was extended exactly from 32 to 128 common-deck pairs per each of six opponents, adding 18,432 environment hands. The original prefix reproduced exactly. Half-cohort rank correlation improved to +0.1190 and 6/8 direction signs agreed in at least three quarters, but mean pairwise quarter rank correlation remained -0.0913 (range -0.6429 to +0.4286). All 266 tests passed.
result.conclusion: Fourfold sampling improves the direction estimator but does not make its ordering reliably reproducible: independent quarter rankings remain anti-correlated on average. Applying the full128 update would violate the preregistered mechanism gate. This is evidence that the current 585-parameter, eight-direction greedy-ES recipe is too sample-inefficient on this hardware/broad league, not evidence that larger training budgets should make every method win Slumbot or that ES is universally invalid.
result.next_step: Close this ES recipe without applying the posthoc full128 direction. Return to methods with per-decision credit and better data efficiency, but require any next scalable route to demonstrate multi-seed geometric slope, broad opponent/seat gains, Standard10 preservation, and proxy/external directional agreement before large allocation.

experiments.title: Calibrated direct-greedy ES minimal signal retry
experiments.benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
experiments.hypothesis: Outcome-blind calibrated sigma 0.8 will activate a reproducible mirrored direct-greedy fitness signal on a wholly new seed: at least one nonzero antithetic difference, positive split-half direction correlation, a nonzero bounded center update, and positive gen0-to-gen1 untouched broad-holdout slope without material Standard10 drift.
experiments.material_change: Repeat only one generation of the state-conditioned ES mechanism on new seed 20262010 using sigma 0.8 selected without rewards. Keep eight directions, six training opponents, both seats, 32 common-deck pairs per opponent, robust fitness, three untouched holdouts, output-only learned weights, residual cap 0.25, and center step L2 0.05. Stop after the minimal 6,144-hand signal gate.
experiments.baseline: Sigma 0.005 produced zero changes over 12,288 hands. Outcome-blind calibration selected sigma 0.8 with 0.83%-1.88% direction-wise greedy disagreement and cap-safe residual logits. No strength evidence exists yet for activated ES.

result.summary: Calibrated sigma 0.8 activated all eight mirrored direct-greedy fitness differences on a wholly new 6,144-hand cohort and produced a nonzero L2=0.05 learned center update. However, independent half-deck direction rankings correlated -0.6313. Untouched broad validation moved -21.3542 bb/100 with CI half-width 41.8542, driven by one holdout and seat1; source agreement remained 99.8535%. All 264 tests passed.
result.conclusion: The perturbation mechanism is now active, but 32 pairs per opponent do not provide a reproducible ES direction: the strongest preregistered signal check is sharply negative and the noisy untouched validation points the same way. This rejects taking a second optimization generation at the current direction-sampling budget. It does not yet reject direct-greedy ES as undertrained, because the causal failure is estimator variance and the validation interval is broad.
result.next_step: Run one fixed-center, no-update direction-SNR scale control at four times the common-deck pairs per opponent. Compare direction rankings across disjoint halves/quarters and against the saved 32-pair cohort. Continue ES only if correlation becomes positive and direction signs stabilize; otherwise close the route as sample-inefficient on current hardware.

experiments.title: Outcome-blind greedy ES sigma calibration
experiments.benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
experiments.hypothesis: The prior zero-signal ES smoke is explained by unit-direction perturbations that were too small to cross Standard10 greedy margins; an outcome-blind geometric sigma scan will identify a cap-safe dose with median 1-8% and target approximately 3% action disagreement across every mirrored direction.
experiments.material_change: Query 4,096 fresh balanced reachable states under the exact Standard10-plus-random-feature residual initialization and the exact eight ES directions. Scan sigma 0.005 through 0.8, measure action disagreement and residual-logit magnitude only, use no rewards or environment outcomes, and select a dose by preregistered activation bounds.
experiments.baseline: At sigma 0.005, two fresh 6,144-hand generations produced exactly zero fitness differences and zero learned-weight update. This calibration determines whether the cause is perturbation scale rather than ES strength.

result.summary: An outcome-blind scan queried the exact eight mirrored ES directions over 4,096 fresh balanced states at eight geometric sigmas. Median greedy disagreement rose from 0 at sigma 0.005 to 1.2695% at sigma 0.8; the selected dose spanned 0.8301%-1.8799% across directions and kept the maximum residual logit near 0.2001 under the 0.25 cap. All 264 tests passed.
result.conclusion: The prior two-generation zero-fitness result was caused by an inactive perturbation dose, not evidence against direct-greedy ES. Sigma 0.8 is the smallest scanned dose satisfying the preregistered 1-8% median activation band with every direction nonzero and cap-safe behavior. This is an outcome-blind activation result only and makes no strength claim.
result.next_step: Run one minimal fresh mirrored generation at sigma 0.8 with the same six opponents and both seats. Require nonzero fitness differences, positive split-half direction correlation, a nonzero trust-region-bounded center update, and untouched holdout direction agreement before considering a second generation or multi-seed geometric scale.

experiments.title: State-conditioned direct-greedy mirrored ES smoke
experiments.benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
experiments.hypothesis: A frozen Standard10 plus a 585-parameter state-conditioned random-feature residual output can obtain a reproducible direct-greedy improvement signal with mirrored common-random-number ES, producing positive gen0-to-gen2 untouched broad-holdout slope in both seats while preserving at least 95% of Standard10 greedy actions.
experiments.material_change: Replace sampled-policy/critic gradient credit with two generations of mirrored parameter-space ES over only the residual policy output layer. Use eight antithetic directions per generation, six heterogeneous training opponents, both seats, fresh generation-specific common decks, robust mean-minus-dispersion fitness, three SHA-disjoint untouched holdouts, a residual logit cap, and fixed center-L2 trust region. No Slumbot or benchmark-specific rules.
experiments.baseline: Standard10 is the only reproducible external frontier parent. PPO/MGDA/CAGrad gradient variants either transferred negatively or lacked multi-seed breadth; a prior 18-dimensional global bias search overfit. This treatment is state-conditioned and directly optimizes the deployed greedy contract.
notes: Method rationale: Salimans et al., Evolution Strategies as a Scalable Alternative to Reinforcement Learning, arXiv:1703.03864. Promotion requires positive split-half direction correlation in both generations, positive untouched validation slopes, two-of-three holdout breadth, both seats, and Standard10 preservation; a small-budget non-win alone is not interpreted as universal algorithm rejection.

result.summary: The direct-greedy mirrored ES smoke completed exactly 12,288 broad training environment hands and 4,608 untouched validation games, but sigma 0.005 never crossed a greedy action boundary: all 16 antithetic fitness differences were exactly zero, both generation updates had L2 zero, the center stayed bit-exact at zero residual, and every validation delta was zero. All 262 tests passed.
result.conclusion: This is a perturbation-dose contract failure, not negative policy-strength evidence. The frozen Standard10 parent and residual remained behaviorally identical with 100% preservation, so the run did not test whether activated state-conditioned ES can learn. The zero signal reproduced on two fresh generation-specific deck cohorts, making further hands at sigma 0.005 wasteful.
result.next_step: Run an outcome-blind state-panel sigma calibration over the exact random-feature output parameterization, targeting a small but nonzero 1-5% greedy disagreement rate while respecting the 0.25 residual cap. Multi-seed breadth and source preservation remain useful necessary filters but are insufficient. This rejects the prior admission protocol, not conflict-aware learning itself nor longer training solely because budgets were <=1M.

Two recoverable implementation interruptions were preserved: one before optimizer step0 due graph reuse, and one after all training but before evaluation due schedule serialization. The accepted run restarted deterministically from the immutable 8k checkpoint and Adam; it did not resume partial optimizer state.

result.summary: The seventh-objective treatment achieved positive alignment for all six reward groups and source KL on 32/32 steps. It strongly improved outcome-blind preservation (panel agreement 99.35% versus control 96.45%; mean KL 0.000240 versus 0.003727), but matched poker performance was pooled -4.553 bb/100 CI[-27.184,18.078], Standard10 -13.306, Slumbot-free +0.916, CFR96 -1.269, with both seat deltas negative.
result.conclusion: Unit-normalizing source KL as a seventh MGDA objective over-constrains useful policy movement: it optimizes the preservation proxy exactly while worsening actual reward breadth, including against Standard10 itself. This is clear mechanism-level evidence to reject this formulation despite small evaluation uncertainty. The unconstrained six-objective control remains a valid 12k continuation artifact and should be evaluated against its 8k parent separately.
result.next_step: Freeze the six-objective 12k control checkpoint and compare it directly with the immutable 8k MGDA parent on new common decks and the existing preservation panel. Post-close implementation audit before the next experiment found that the smoke's passive initializer zeroed every network parameter. This preserved passive behavior but created a dead/symmetry-limited ReLU feature stack, so the zero argmax movement cannot isolate optimizer dose. The next matched control uses seeded random hidden features with only the final outputs set passive; the original checkpoint/result/decision remain unchanged.

result.summary: The bounded learned-weight run completed 8 roots and 29,093 exact-v6 nodes with finite losses and exact checkpoint reload, but 32 optimizer steps produced only about 0.08 TV probability movement and zero greedy argmax flips across 2,048 untouched evaluation hands.
result.conclusion: The adapter and serialization remain healthy, but this optimization dose does not establish meaningful learned behavior. Wide 512-hand anchor returns are non-decisive and are not used to admit scaling.
result.next_step: Freeze and serialize one first-iteration target corpus, then compare 32/128/512 optimizer-step arms from identical passive weights using held-out target loss and frozen-state argmax/TV movement before adding traversal volume.

result.summary: The direct ChipState external-sampling adapter passed every mechanism gate on 16 unique alternating-seat roots: 48,016 decisions, 37,352 terminal rollouts, 2,672 finite masked targets per traverser, exact shared action slots/transitions, zero-sum BB payoffs, and opponent-hole encoding invariance.
result.conclusion: Exact physical-v6 CFR traversal is feasible without the legacy HUNL rules engine. The evidence admits a bounded neural regret optimization smoke, but does not yet establish learning quality or count as environment training hands.
result.next_step: Run a deterministic small neural-regret optimization with explicit root-deal/node accounting; require healthy target/loss distributions, checkpoint reload parity, nontrivial behavioral movement, and untouched evaluation against fixed exact-v6 policies before scaling.

experiments.title: Deep CFR physical-v6 readiness audit
experiments.benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
experiments.hypothesis: The existing Deep CFR core may be algorithmically functional on Leduc, but its HUNL game/export wiring is not yet contract-compatible with exact 200bb physical-v6 and therefore should not receive a large training budget until explicit parity gates pass.
experiments.material_change: Add a deterministic, no-training-hand readiness audit comparing Deep CFR game/action/export surfaces with physical-v6 and run a cheap exact tabular Leduc convergence control.

The preregistered 200-iteration tabular control ended at 165.3158 mbb/game after a nonmonotone 100-to-200 segment; extend the no-HUNL-hand control to 1000 iterations to distinguish insufficient small-game budget from a broken regret core.

The first direct launch exposed a repository-root import bootstrap omission before the audit ran; the same preregistered command succeeded after adding only SCRIPTS_ROOT to sys.path. No poker hands or partial result artifact were produced by the failed launch.

result.summary: Exact audit generated zero HUNL training/evaluation hands. Tabular Leduc converged to 26.1112 mbb/game at 1000 iterations, but all five physical-HUNL gates failed: trainer and CLI omit full_200bb, initial action slots differ, postflop re-raises are blocked, and nine-action checkpoints cannot load into the hardcoded six-action exporter.
result.conclusion: The regret core is viable enough to justify an exact-v6 adapter experiment, but the existing HUNL trainer cannot train or export the target physical-v6 game without silently changing the game or failing on shapes.
result.next_step: Implement and parity-test a minimal external-sampling traversal adapter directly over ChipState and policy_contract_v6.action_table; require exact transition/action/payoff gates plus a tiny bounded traversal smoke before any larger neural regret training.

result.summary: The admitted 64-row history-consistent posterior was evaluated with disjoint 8+8 opponent-hole/future samples across every legal action, producing 7,776 continuation rollouts. experiments.title: Outcome-blind iter16 versus parent Slumbot-state drift decomposition
experiments.benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
experiments.hypothesis: The externally losing iter16 checkpoint differs from Standard10 on a small, identifiable high-leverage subset of actual Slumbot states rather than through broad diffuse drift; comparing candidate-onpolicy and parent-onpolicy state corpora can locate the context without using hand outcomes as labels.
experiments.material_change: Replay exact parent and iter16 policies on every audited decision response from the independent parent fresh20k and candidate fresh20k cohorts. Compute probabilities, physical greedy actions, margins and outcome-blind context strata by street, seat, pot, SPR, facing-bet and parent action class. Do not read winnings or train.
experiments.baseline: Synthetic four-street drift at iter16 was mean TV 0.02390 and 3.008% greedy disagreement, while fresh20k transfer was -37.1617 versus parent -24.5683. The internal multi-anchor proxy incorrectly promoted iter16.
notes: Outcome and cumulative winnings fields are deliberately not accessed. This is descriptive allocation evidence, not training data or strength evidence.

The initial GPU-batched analysis marked FAIL because 4/122,875 logged argmax actions differed. Independent CPU-single replay matched all four live actions; maximum GPU margin was 0.000352. Original analysis/raw remain unchanged and the backend audit documents the correction.

result.summary: Outcome-blind replay queried parent and iter16 on 122,875 audited Slumbot decision states from independent parent/candidate cohorts. Both corpora showed stable broad drift: about 0.0224 mean TV and 3.30% greedy disagreement, amplified to 5.23-5.44% when weighted by pot plus call exposure.
result.conclusion: The small-isolated-context hypothesis is rejected. Drift is consistent across both on-policy corpora and amplified in high-leverage states: facing-bet 4.84%, river 5.67%, >=30bb pots 7.20% on candidate states, with major fold-to-call, call-to-raise and raise-to-fold transitions. A local benchmark-specific rule would not address this. Standard source KL preserves average probability but not high-stake greedy actions; the next learned-weight intervention should weight preservation by public-state risk and source margin while retaining advantage-based release.
result.next_step: Implement a default-off, generic risk-weighted source-greedy preservation objective using only public pot/to-call/effective-stack features and the frozen Standard10 reference. Verify gradient/tensor scope in a matched smoke, then run a matched 65k control only if it reduces stake-weighted greedy disagreement without freezing all learning. Do not use Slumbot outcomes or identities in training.

experiments.material_change: Generate deterministic general-policy v6 trajectories with no Slumbot outcomes, reconstruct each live decision under the frozen Standard10 v4/preflop_pot_fraction_v2 contract, map its chosen physical action to the nearest legal v6 action, and compare against the same weights rebound to v6. No environment training hands and no network calls.
experiments.baseline: Historical Standard10 old-contract greedy fresh20k -11.4275 bb/100 CI[-28.7124,5.8574]; exact v6 rebound greedy fresh5k -96.6832 bb/100. Single imitation-teacher fresh20k -18.5025 is explicitly non-supportive.
notes: Outcome-blind preregistration. If state reconstruction or physical-action mapping fails its gate, finish without training. Do not infer strength from agreement alone.

result.summary: Deterministic four-street 50,000-state general v6 simulation established exact old-parser state parity, 100% old-action legal mappability, and zero physical sizing error. The same learned tensors nevertheless agreed on only 86.742% of greedy actions after v6 rebinding, dominated by preflop agreement of 61.04%; postflop agreement was 94.02%-97.19%. Independent raw-row/hash audit passed.
result.conclusion: The historical Standard10 clue is identifiable and execution-contract-specific: physical rules and action tables are not the source of the loss; v4-versus-v6 observation semantics, especially preflop action-history encoding, materially change decisions from identical learned weights. This does not prove strength and does not overturn the negative -18.5025 imitation-teacher result.
result.next_step: Implement a generic frozen inference bridge that reconstructs the audited v4 observation from v6 ChipState and verify exact parity against the old deployment path on deterministic states. Only if exact should it receive one small fresh greedy Slumbot calibration; do not train an imitation policy first.

experiments.benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
experiments.hypothesis: The 65k treatment became overdosed only after an earlier archived checkpoint that still delivers material contextual correction within the 0.05 source-preservation envelope; selecting that boundary without reward evidence can separate dose failure from direction failure.

experiments.baseline: Iter2 isolated smoke passed at overall TV/disagreement 0.01245/0.01043; independent iter16 pilot failed at 0.06377/0.08378. Iter16 learned panel was inconclusive and is not used for dose selection.

Independent review PASS: all eight dose points were recomputed from stored probability arrays with archive hashes; iter4 selection reproduced; all 6,144 selected-panel raw pairs/decks/CIs reproduced. Allocation gate failed, so no Slumbot hands.

result.summary: Outcome-blind replay selected iter4 as the last even checkpoint inside the 0.05 preservation envelope; iter6 first failed disagreement. The single untouched iter4 panel then scored -8.26 bb/100 treatment-control, CI[-27.15,10.63], with only 1/3 anchors positive.

Use the accumulated evidence to choose a value/action-credit or genuine opponent-league/self-play learned-weight intervention that can improve per-state decisions without forcing aggregate class frequencies; retain preflop-head-only topology only as a diagnostic isolation tool.

Mechanism gate is outcome-blind on the frozen source Slumbot state corpus: treatment must reduce excessive contextual greedy raise mass/frequency versus matched control, keep postflop treatment-minus-control mean TV within 0.005, and keep overall source-parent TV/disagreement at or below 0.02. No Slumbot performance test from this smoke.
Matched control reached iter2 with 8,775 physical/8,260 transition hands, fresh optimizer, max displayed source KL 0.0012 and zero KL stops.
Both fixed-pool session audits PASS; optimizer steps are matched at 60 and both assignment chains contain exactly two verified rows.

result.summary: Matched 8k-per-arm smoke completed 17,542 physical hands. Context priors reduced SB greedy raise frequency from 99.83% to 99.38% and BB-vs-open from 94.98% to 89.80%; overall treatment-parent TV/disagreement stayed 0.01718/0.01610, but postflop treatment-control TV was 0.02031 versus the preregistered 0.005 ceiling.
result.conclusion: The contextual prior is a real and directionally useful preflop gradient signal, especially for BB defense, but all-policy-head PPO changes the postflop head enough that the preregistered isolation gate fails. This endpoint is not eligible for scaling or Slumbot evaluation.
result.next_step: Implement and unit-test a preflop-head-only training mode that freezes the postflop policy head and shared trunk, then repeat the matched 8k mechanism smoke. Admit a larger pilot only if postflop execution is exactly preserved while contextual raise collapse improves.

A separately logged direct fresh Slumbot cohort is allowed only for the frozen matched endpoints and must compare both arms; no 100k qualification from this pilot.

Control frozen at the preregistered physical threshold endpoint iter16: 68,029 physical/66,033 transition hands, optimizer step464, max source KL0.004724, zero stops; session audit PASS with16 archives and16 exact assignment records.

Treatment frozen at iter16: 67,976 physical/65,923 transition hands, optimizer step480, max source KL0.003514, zero stops; session audit PASS. Both arms changed only the same ten allowed tensors and their 16 local-index assignment schedules are exactly equal.

Untouched 6,144-pair learned panel: pooled treatment-control -0.0594 bb/100 CI[-22.0376,21.9187],1/3 positive. Per-anchor deltas Standard10 -14.4275, slumbot_free -3.8694, CFR96 +18.1187; all paired CIs cross zero.

result.summary: Matched soup-initialized 65k arms completed 136,005 physical training hands with exact assignment control. Diverse learned opponents gave pooled -0.0594 bb/100 CI[-22.0376,21.9187], only1/3 positive anchors, and worsened source-state drift to TV0.02208/disagreement0.02421 versus control0.01951/0.01998.
result.conclusion: Replacing duplicate-soup opponent slots with the selected diverse current-v6 pool produced no detectable generalization gain and crossed the source-state preservation boundary. Learned-opponent diversity at this scale/distribution is rejected; no Slumbot hands are allocated to the treatment.
result.next_step: Do not scale or externally test the diversity treatment. The duplicate-soup mixed-curriculum control independently passed the outcome-blind <=0.02 source-state preservation thresholds and was not selected by internal performance; log one exploratory fresh5k current-v6 greedy transfer cohort for that frozen control. Only a credible direct improvement over the soup's -41.8162 fresh20k reference may justify confirmation.

result.summary: The same frozen raw actor completed eight fixed fresh625 generic-greedy sessions. All 5000 hands passed captured-runtime, learned-logit argmax, terminal, server-counter, token-chain, and independent raw evidence review. Terminal ledger artifact registration was recovered in batches after a Windows command-length error; no session reran.
result.conclusion: Generic greedy execution improved the same checkpoint point estimate by 69.7938 bb/100 versus its separate sampled pilot and reached -9.4188 bb/100, close to historical Standard10 greedy. Greedy is the correct current deployment direction, but this policy is not admitted to 20k or qualification.

Train a matched low-entropy actor-head treatment from Standard10 to test whether removing stochastic-entropy pressure sharpens learned action margins without imitation; gate first on untouched anchors and preserved Slumbot-state entropy/TV, then spend fresh hands only if it improves both mechanism and internal reward.

experiments.title: Preserved Slumbot-state policy-distribution diagnostic
experiments.benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
experiments.hypothesis: The raw actor's external failure is associated with a concentrated, reproducible policy-distribution drift from the near-zero Standard10 reference on particular street/seat partitions.

notes: Preregistered before implementation. No outcome labels, network calls, or weight changes.

result.summary: Offline batched replay compared raw and rebound-Standard10 distributions on all 15056 audited fresh5k decision states; independent aggregation and input hashes passed with zero network calls.
result.conclusion: No supported street-seat partition crossed the preregistered 0.10 TV or 25% greedy-disagreement threshold. Overall drift was modest (TV 0.0573, disagreement 6.62%); the largest preflop seat0 shift reduced slot2 probability by 0.066 and increased slot1 by 0.039. A single localized actor-head drift does not explain the external failure, and the raw-policy on-policy corpus cannot estimate counterfactual source value.
result.next_step: Do not add a local action correction or imitation loss. The highest-information next control is a small same-checkpoint greedy-versus-sampled execution comparison under a newly audited generic greedy journal contract, because historical Standard10 evidence shows a large contract gap and the current state-distribution drift is diffuse.

experiments.title: Conservative all-legal counterfactual soft-policy pilot
experiments.benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
experiments.hypothesis: A bounded non-one-hot policy target built from paired common-random-number all-legal action advantages, with uncertainty-conservative LCB targets and row-only reliability weighting, will provide lower-variance alternative-action supervision and improve robust policy strength without the chosen-action Q bias that failed historically.
experiments.material_change: First decouple policy-only counterfactual distillation from the Action-Q head so no Q values enter rollout action selection. Build one immutable balanced BB/SB x flop/turn dataset by strictly merging the existing 10,240-row paired-CRN partial dataset with its 512-row SB-turn shard. Relative to the untouched all-heads control, enable only bounded soft-policy replay at coefficient 0.01, advantage_lcb z=1.96, row_only reliability, one 512-row replay batch per update, and linear decay to zero over 262,144 hands. Keep lambda 0.95 and all other control seeds, deals, league, architecture, and PPO settings.
experiments.baseline: adaptive-league-all-heads-pilot-20260830 untouched on-policy all-policy-heads control
experiments.source: Legacy exact Action-Q and one-step hard/capped selectors failed, but the current paired-uncertainty loader and bounded soft-policy objective provide a distinct conservative all-legal target; the available partial data plus SB-turn shard cover all four seat/street cells and five trajectory styles.

Strict dataset merge and loader audit must show 10,752 rows, all BB/SB x flop/turn x five trajectory strata, paired anchor-action uncertainty, held-out train/validation/test split, and immutable SHA256. A 4,096-hand smoke must show positive finite soft-policy loss, exactly one replay batch, finite PPO metrics, no KL stop, and terminal audit PASS. Production only on PASS; four-checkpoint seed20260853 paired curve versus untouched control; no Slumbot without robust direction-consistent evidence.
Policy-only decoupling tests PASS 2/2: soft replay backpropagates into policy logits without any Action-Q interface/head and advances the deterministic replay cursor exactly once per batch.

Dataset gate PASS: strict full-schema merge produced immutable SHA256 605a7ab8...efb8e with 10,752 rows. Live loader produced 6,454 train / 2,149 validation / 2,149 test rows; all 20 seat-street-trajectory strata were nonempty in every split; paired-CRN advantage LCB z=1.96 and conservative five-continuation uncertainty were active.

Smoke gate PASS at 4,103 actual hands: policy-only soft loss was finite and positive (0.2573), counterfactual Q loss exactly zero, Action-Q architecture disabled, exactly one 512-row replay batch applied, source KL 0.00008367, zero clip/stop, and fixed-pool terminal audit PASS.
Policy-only replay auditor validated on the completed one-update smoke evidence while the untouched production session continued; no training source, checkpoint, optimizer, or cursor was modified.
Production completed without interruption at 263,417 actual hands. Fixed-pool assignment/session audit and policy-only replay cursor/decay audit both passed before any frozen evaluation.

result.summary: Policy-only uncertainty-conservative counterfactual replay completed valid smoke and 263,417-hand production, but its frozen matched curve had only 5/12 positive deltas, mean -0.414 and median -0.229 bb/100, with every paired interval crossing zero.
result.conclusion: The treatment is mechanically valid and stable but did not robustly improve general strength over the untouched adaptive-league all-heads control at this dataset size and coefficient.
result.next_step: Select a materially broader learned-policy data or optimization intervention; do not scale this small offline counterfactual treatment unchanged and do not spend Slumbot hands on it.

experiments.title: Monte-Carlo hand-return GAE pilot
experiments.benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.

experiments.title: Matched one-board CFR i800 convergence control
experiments.benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
experiments.hypothesis: For the exact board0/config/seed used by the i200 teacher, recomputing SRP and 3BP to i800 will materially reduce shallow-node strategy drift relative to i50-to-i200; if shallow drift remains high, CFR targets should not be confidence-weighted or scaled from i200.
experiments.material_change: Re-solve the exact As-7d-2c board0 from zero at b8/i800 for deployment_v55_srp_200bb and deployment_v55_3bp_200bb with seed 20260829, because the solver does not serialize regrets and --resume only skips completed boards. Compare deterministic sampled i200-to-i800 strategy drift by street/depth using the existing primary-source comparison code.
experiments.baseline: cfr-convergence-confidence-audit-20260830: i50-to-i200 mean TV 0.069 SRP and 0.080 3BP; 18.4%/21.9% of rows exceed TV 0.1, with 3BP shallow roots especially unstable.
experiments.source: cfr-convergence-confidence-audit-20260830 decision DEEPEN_ONE_BOARD_BEFORE_CONFIDENCE_WEIGHTING; exact i200 metadata in deployment-cfr8-deep-20260829.
notes: No learned policy is changed in this convergence control. Promotion criterion: i200-to-i800 shallow/root drift must be materially below i50-to-i200 on both SRP and 3BP before any convergence-weighted distillation. Solver --resume is intentionally not used because no regret-state continuation exists.

A prior attempt to invoke solve.ts with --help revealed that the CLI has no help mode and briefly launched legacy defaults. Exact PID 41468 was terminated at iter0/0 infosets; the default output directory contained no files afterward, so it contributes zero samples and no artifact.

SRP i800 completed from zero on the exact matched board/config/seed: 22,703,360 infosets, 623.6s solve, 693.3s including 1.257GB JSONL export. Starting matched 3BP i800 serially to avoid resource contention.

3BP i800 completed from zero: 3,673,670 infosets, 123.1s solve, 133.6s including 195.8MB export. Starting deterministic 0.002 sampled matched i200-to-i800 comparisons; all flop histories at depth <=1 are included regardless of sampling.

Both trees show consistent 36-39% shallow mean-TV reductions from i50->i200 to i200->i800, but absolute drift remains too high for confidence weighting: 7/8 root buckets in each tree still exceed TV 0.1. ALL-row drift is not a convergence estimator because i800 expands reachable support substantially.

result.summary: Exact matched board0 b8/i800 recomputes produced 22,703,360 SRP and 3,673,670 3BP infosets. Shallow mean TV fell by 36-39% versus the earlier i50-to-i200 interval, but root instability remained high (87.5% of buckets above TV 0.1 in both trees).
result.conclusion: More CFR iterations consistently reduce shallow drift, but i200 and even i800 are not sufficiently stable to justify checkpoint-drift confidence weights. The deeper artifacts are useful higher-fidelity teacher data; these measurements are strategy drift only, not exploitability.
result.next_step: Use the i800 board0 artifacts only as higher-fidelity supervision/control. Before scaling CFR breadth, test whether replacing the unstable i200 board0 targets with i800 targets yields a measurable learned-policy gain under a bounded matched distillation experiment, without treating drift as calibrated confidence.

result.summary: Implemented and audited identity-safe seeded dynamic K-best training, completed 263,581 actual environment hands, and evaluated four frozen checkpoints on 24,576 fresh internal hands against an untouched matched control.
result.conclusion: The infrastructure and training run succeeded: dynamic membership, adaptive weights, assignment RNG provenance, optimizer state, and four checkpoint hashes all passed audit; two learned snapshots survived K-best selection and the policy stayed inside the source trust region. Iter64 produced a narrow positive Standard10 delta and a positive but inconclusive slumbot_free point estimate, while CFR96 remained negative and inconclusive.
result.next_step: Do not scale this proxy K-best curriculum. Run exactly one independent-deal-seed matched replication of frozen iter64 versus the same frozen fresh-only iter64 control; if lower-variance anchors do not replicate positive direction, retire this route.
